ours.finding: Native provider tools and conductors plus cross-runtime hooks. This is several integrations, not one provider-neutral execution engine. A Grok model-label mismatch was observed in the fleet controller.

omnara.finding: Provider-neutral configuration supports Responses, Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages. Production egress rejects loopback, LAN and tailnet addresses; local-model compatibility requires an appropriately reachable endpoint, not merely a compatible API.

ours.finding: Operation receipts, durable jobs and native conductor history exist. No single transaction spans model state, the memory layer, fleet ownership and external side effects.

omnara.finding: Postgres-backed execution state, runtime locks and explicit ambiguous model-call recovery. This does not guarantee exactly-once effects at an external tool.

ours.finding: Native conductor start, steer and interrupt; connector predecessor handoff retains resident handles. Portability across runtimes is uneven.

omnara.finding: Queued versus steering input, cancellation and retained conversation are first-class. Archive is terminal; it is not a reversible pause.

ours.finding: Native agents, leased Inbox messages, versioned assignments and Beads dependencies. Native delivery and actual work acceptance remain separate.

omnara.finding: Configurable child-agent tools, parent IDs, messaging and timelines. Human interactions are separate from parent responses.

ours.finding: Explicit SSH enrollment, identity-pinned fleet tool discovery and host-local resources. The deployed connector and the seven-host orchestration estate are different scopes.

omnara.finding: Outbound machine daemon and agents using several BYO or pooled machines. Runtime and persistent state are separated.

ours.finding: No first-class multi-provider sandbox pool lifecycle found in the inspected BORG distribution. Generic shell or SSH extensibility is not counted as the feature.

omnara.finding: Blaxel, Daytona, Modal and Unikraft provider implementations, pool/project limits, provisioning and cleanup. Remote-provider acceptance was not run.

ours.finding: Native macOS UI and browser tooling, session/resource locks and operating-system permission boundaries. A physical desktop still has one focus.

omnara.finding: No built-in native desktop or browser interaction surface found in the inspected tool catalog and implementations. Web search/fetch and shell execution are different capabilities. External MCP/browser automation remains an integration path.

ours.finding: Authenticated MCP gateway, live capability discovery, native CLI and skill/catalog access. Source and runtime tool sets need reconciliation.

omnara.finding: HTTP MCP with OAuth/bearer/SigV4, deferred discovery, custom tools and versioned skill packages. Some permission defaults differ by tool type.

ours.finding: Scoped cross-session semantic recall is implemented and the native memory search returned relevant candidates in this audit. That does not prove recall quality for every workload.

omnara.finding: No built-in cross-agent semantic store found in agent config, tools, storage and docs. Conversation history and compaction are present; external MCP memory is possible.

ours.finding: Graph scope validation, current-only filtering and provenance-aware candidates exist. Live graph status passed but ingestion watermark and last complete scan were null.

omnara.finding: No built-in temporal entity/relation graph or provenance-qualified shared recall found. An event timeline is a different capability.

ours.finding: Hooks, bounded selection, guarded consolidation and retention plans are implemented. Semantic-preservation effectiveness was not measured here.

omnara.finding: Context compaction and artifact/event persistence exist. Shared semantic consolidation and memory lifecycle were not found.

ours.finding: Pinned local extraction models and exam/canary training workflow. Included LoRA students remain benched or limited; no autonomous self-improvement claim is justified.

omnara.finding: Can use compatible local model endpoints; no extraction-model training or promotion workflow found.

ours.finding: Several native consoles and a telemetry dashboard exist. A unified, independently installable execution/approval/cost console was not demonstrated.

omnara.finding: Integrated agent conversations, configuration builder, streamed events, approvals and usage views in the web application. Source-level UX audit only.

ours.finding: Memory scopes, Inbox principals/grants and cloud tenants protect distinct surfaces. They do not form one consistent org/project/operator/viewer product contract.

omnara.finding: Explicit organization and project roles, resource grants and separately scoped API identities. Role matrix is implemented in authz.

ours.finding: Owner authentication, scope gates, value-blind credential handles and native holds. Broad native shell access remains a trusted-owner boundary, not a sandbox.

omnara.finding: Tool allow/ask/deny, canonical authorized arguments, first-writer-wins interactions and secret references. Built-in/custom tools default allow; integration messaging only supports allow.

ours.finding: Native hooks, scheduled memory jobs and platform automation exist across separate components. Cross-provider delivery is not one portable contract.

omnara.finding: Cron triggers, event streams, webhooks and first-party Slack integration have dedicated implementation and tests.

ours.finding: Physical-resource measurements and native work claims are present. This run observed complete raw fleet measurements but failed aggregate fleet-context coverage and controller version drift.

omnara.finding: Pool CPU/memory and machine-count caps, grants and runtime locks. No equivalent measured seven-host workload placement and independent work-ownership authority found.

ours.finding: Provider-specific account/allowance routing and recovery machinery. It remains separate from machine capacity, and this audit exposed compatibility friction before useful Grok work.

omnara.finding: Provider configuration and bounded model retries exist; a subscription-seat allowance rotation and original-native-task recovery system was not found.

ours.finding: Local metadata ledger, provider-specific telemetry, source-qualified token dimensions and reported/estimated/unknown costs. Native status command timed out; no current full-coverage claim.

omnara.finding: Model-usage storage, provider-reported costs and project/org/profile views. Includes coverage counts; not equivalent to provider invoice reconciliation.

ours.finding: GitHub linkage, immutable outcomes, first-pass yield and cost/acceptance contracts exist. Complete economic attribution and causal ROI are not established by source or telemetry.

omnara.finding: Queryable execution and usage can feed analytics; no built-in PR/check/mature-acceptance or cost-per-validated-outcome join found.

ours.finding: Metadata suppression before persistence, hashed identity, scoped recall and future-only enrollment contracts. This is metadata minimization, not universal zero-sensitive-data certification.

omnara.finding: Access control and secret boundaries exist, while event/tool content is retained for execution and analytics. No comparable metadata-only telemetry collection mode found.

ours.finding: Durable operation receipts and acceptance/evidence contracts; callers must inspect uncertain outcomes before retry. Forty-one focused connector tests passed; not a whole-stack guarantee.

omnara.finding: Transactional state, idempotent input/interaction resolution and explicit ambiguous recovery states. External side-effect semantics still require an adapter contract.

ours.finding: Independent owner installer and local-first collector. Apple Silicon is the verified installer target; Linux/Intel full acceptance and Plimsoll paid-cloud launch remain qualified.

omnara.finding: Documented Compose control plane and BYO daemon; operational dependencies include Postgres, Redis and blob storage. Fresh installation not tested in this audit.

ours.finding: Public source, native CLI/MCP, installer guides and component licenses. Multiple repositories and runtime/source drift create integration work for adopters.

omnara.finding: OpenAPI, generated TypeScript client/CLI, examples and contribution gates create a more unified developer entry point. Production support quality not measured.

axes.name: Managed execution
axes.reason: Omnara provides a unified transactional agent lifecycle; ours composes native runtimes and receipts.

axes.name: Collective memory
axes.reason: Our explicit semantic and temporal recall exceeds conversation persistence; quality and freshness still need measurement.

axes.name: Fleet operations
axes.reason: We measure physical hosts and ownership; Omnara has cleaner pool lifecycle. Our model-label drift is a current usability defect.

axes.name: Delivery economics
axes.reason: Plimsoll adds outcome/coverage contracts, while neither source audit proves causal ROI or fully reconciled billing.

axes.name: Product readiness
axes.reason: Omnara has a cohesive API/dashboard. BORG and Plimsoll have distinct install and launch boundaries.

recommendations.title: Reuse Omnara interaction and timeline patterns in one operational view
recommendations.risk: A viewer must preserve native authority and must not introduce a second work-state owner.

recommendations.title: Pilot Omnara as an optional managed execution backend
recommendations.risk: API billing, event privacy, identity mapping and external-effect replay differ from native subscription tasks.

recommendations.title: Borrow machine-pool lifecycle for isolated disposable work
recommendations.risk: Cloud sandbox costs, cleanup failures and native-desktop incompatibility; avoid migrating working host tasks.

recommendations.title: Offer a scoped BORG memory MCP reference integration
recommendations.risk: Never expose owner-wide memory or private training data; enforce per-project scope and provenance.

recommendations.title: Add a Plimsoll adapter for Omnara usage and accepted outcomes
recommendations.risk: Stable event identities and missing-cost coverage must survive retries; token dimensions cannot be double-counted.

recommendations.title: Supply optional measured BYO-host admission and ownership checks
recommendations.risk: Do not turn stale telemetry or soft policy into universal enforcement; keep one native authority.

limitations: Source audit is not a production penetration test, load benchmark or customer acceptance.
No Omnara deployment or provider sandbox was started. Focused Go tests were blocked by installed Go 1.25.6 versus required 1.27.1.
BORG connector liveness and Mem0 recall were observed; graph ingestion watermark and last complete scan were null.
Forty-one focused BORG connector tests passed; they cover concurrency, process handoff and independent settings only.
Plimsoll tracked working-tree snapshot contains uncommitted work; its native status read was stopped after exceeding 150 seconds. Paid cloud readiness is not asserted.
Runtime memory source has capabilities beyond the public BORG snapshot. No private implementation or records are offered for contribution automatically.
Scores are this auditor's judgment under the common rubric, not benchmarks; missing capabilities mean not found in the inspected scope.
citation_refinement: Directory-level citations narrowed to existing files after initial seal; no ratings or findings changed.

post_seal_corrections.reason: Pre-review self-check: generic shell/web tools and future MCP extensibility must not receive credit for implemented native desktop/browser interaction. Source finding unchanged; rubric applied more strictly.
After Opus review, verified production network restrictions and qualified local-endpoint compatibility.
